pictures.name: header
pictures.alt: Illustration seen from above: a marble track dug into sand, from a raised start at the top through banked bends and a splitter round a mound to a finish pit, with marbles racing down it.
pictures.caption: A marble track in the sand, from the start to the finish pit. Illustration.

pictures.name: what-you-need
pictures.alt: Illustration of what you need: a spade, a bucket, a watering can, a flat piece of wood or a ruler, and a few marbles.
pictures.caption: A spade, a bucket, a watering can, something flat and a few marbles. Illustration.

pictures.name: pick-the-spot
pictures.alt: Illustration of a long sandy slope seen from the side, with an arrow down it: damp sand holds its shape best, and the longer the slope, the more fun.
pictures.caption: Any sandy slope will do; damp sand holds its shape best. Illustration.

pictures.name: dig
pictures.alt: Diagram of the channel cut across: a rounded groove about two marbles wide with a raised wall of sand on each side, two marbles side by side in it, and a spade piling sand along the edges.
pictures.caption: The channel: about two marbles wide, with raised walls on both sides. Diagram.

pictures.name: water
pictures.alt: Illustration of a watering can pouring water over the channel and its walls so the sand sticks together.
pictures.caption: Wet the floor and the walls, then wait a minute. Illustration.

pictures.name: smooth
pictures.alt: Diagram comparing two channels cut across: on the left a bumpy floor, marked wrong; on the right a smooth floor patted flat with a piece of wood, marked right.
pictures.caption: Pat the floor and walls smooth, so the marbles roll and don't jump out. Diagram.

pictures.name: start
pictures.alt: Illustration of the start seen from the side: a raised sand platform at the top of the slope with four marbles side by side behind a stick, and a straight run-in down from it.
pictures.caption: A raised start with a straight run-in: lift the stick and every marble gets a fair start. Illustration.

pictures.name: banked-bend
pictures.alt: Diagram of a banked bend: seen from above, the channel turns with its outside wall built higher, and a marble follows the bend; cut across, the outside wall stands higher than the inside one.
pictures.caption: Build the outside wall of each bend higher so the marbles stay in. Diagram.

pictures.name: splitter
pictures.alt: Diagram seen from above: the channel splits in two round a mound of sand and the two channels join again after it, with marbles taking each way.
pictures.caption: A splitter: two channels round a mound, the same length and slope, or one side always wins. Diagram.

pictures.name: finish
pictures.alt: Illustration seen from above: the channel ends in a round finish pit dug in the sand, with a dashed finish line and a chequered flag before it.
pictures.caption: A finish line and a pit that catches the marbles. Illustration.

pictures.name: race
pictures.alt: Illustration seen from above: four marbles racing down a winding sand track, numbered by their places, with the rules beside it: everyone picks a marble, all start together, first in the pit wins.
pictures.caption: Pick a marble, start together, first in the pit wins. Then build it longer. Illustration.

pictures.name: share
pictures.alt: Build a marble track in the sand. Illustrated marbles: a cat's eye, a corkscrew, an oxblood and a clearie.
